runbooks.title: Memory Exhaustion / OOMKilled
steps: Step 1: Run check_metrics to identify which service has MEM >90%.
Step 2: Run query_logs on the affected service filtering for 'ERROR' or 'OutOfMemory'.
Step 3: Run run_diagnostic with tool=heap_dump on the affected service to identify what is consuming memory.
Step 4: If heap dump shows unbounded cache → apply_fix fix_type=patch_cache_config.
Step 5: If heap dump shows memory limit is just too low → apply_fix fix_type=increase_memory_limit (temporary workaround – schedule proper fix).
Step 6: Acknowledge related alerts.
Step 7: Monitor for 5 minutes to confirm memory stabilises.
Step 8: mark_resolved with root cause referencing heap dump findings.
common_root_causes: Unbounded in-memory cache (no maxSize or TTL configured)
Memory leak in request handling (objects not GC'd)
Memory limit set too low for current traffic volume
Sudden traffic spike exhausting normal allocation
do_not: Do NOT increase memory limit as a first response without diagnosing root cause.
Do NOT restart the service without capturing a heap dump first – you will lose the evidence.
Do NOT scale horizontally if the issue is a memory leak – you will OOM all replicas.

runbooks.title: Database Performance Degradation / Slow Queries
steps: Step 1: Run check_metrics – look for DB service CPU >80% or high p99 latency.
Step 2: Run query_logs on the database service filtering for 'slow query' or 'timeout'.
Step 3: Run run_diagnostic with tool=explain_query on the database to see query plans.
Step 4: Run run_diagnostic with tool=check_migrations to check for failed or stuck migrations.
Step 5: If INVALID index found → apply_fix fix_type=reindex_invalid_index (preferred) or drop_invalid_index (emergency).
Step 6: If missing index → create index (schedule during maintenance window).
Step 7: If connection pool exhausted → investigate which upstream service is holding connections.
Step 8: Do NOT restart the DB without DBA approval – data loss risk.
Step 9: mark_resolved with root cause referencing query plan or migration status.
common_root_causes: Failed CONCURRENT index build leaving INVALID index (falls back to Seq Scan)
N+1 query pattern introduced in recent deployment
Connection pool exhaustion from upstream scaling
do_not: Do NOT restart postgres without DBA approval.
Do NOT scale upstream services horizontally during DB saturation – it makes connection exhaustion worse.
Do NOT DROP an index without understanding why it exists.

runbooks.title: DDoS / Volumetric Attack on API Endpoints
steps: Step 1: Run check_metrics to confirm traffic spike and identify affected endpoints.
Step 2: Run query_logs on api-gateway filtering for 'WAF' or 'rate limit'.
Step 3: Run run_diagnostic with tool=waf_rules to see current protection rules.
Step 4: Apply apply_fix fix_type=rate_limit_auth_endpoint to throttle the attacking IPs.
Step 5: Run run_diagnostic with tool=network_capture to identify source IP ranges.
Step 6: Apply apply_fix fix_type=block_tor_subnet if attack originates from known bad IP ranges.
Step 7: CRITICAL – Check ALL other alerts simultaneously. DDoS is often a distraction for a secondary attack.
Step 8: Run query_logs on internal services (data-pipeline, user-db) for anomalous activity.
Step 9: If secondary attack detected → escalate to security team IMMEDIATELY.
Step 10: Preserve forensic evidence before any cleanup.
Step 11: mark_resolved – document both the attack vector AND any secondary activity found.
common_root_causes: Credential stuffing botnet (rotating IPs, user-agent spoofing)
DDoS-as-distraction for data exfiltration (HIGH RISK – check secondary alerts)
do_not: Do NOT focus exclusively on the DDoS without investigating other simultaneous alerts.
Do NOT clean up logs or network captures before forensics are preserved.
Do NOT block all traffic to the endpoint – legitimate users will be impacted.

runbooks.title: Gradual Memory / CPU Trend Toward Failure (Proactive Prevention)
steps: Step 1: Run get_metric_trends on the suspect service to confirm the trend (window_minutes=30 recommended).
Step 2: Calculate projected time-to-failure: current_value + (rate_per_minute * remaining_minutes).
Step 3: Run query_logs to look for early warning signs (WARN level entries, increasing error counts).
Step 4: Run run_diagnostic to understand root cause before it becomes critical.
Step 5: File a prediction using predict_incident with your predicted failure type and confidence.
Step 6: Apply a proactive fix BEFORE the threshold is breached.
Step 7: Set a proactive alert using set_proactive_alert so the team is notified if trend continues.
Step 8: mark_resolved documenting the trend, predicted failure, and preventive action taken.
common_root_causes: Memory leak slowly accumulating (cache, connection pool, event listeners)
Slow-burning query plan regression after index statistics update
Certificate/token approaching expiry causing increasing auth failures
do_not: Do NOT wait for an alert to fire if trends clearly indicate imminent failure.
Do NOT apply fixes without diagnosing root cause first – proactive does not mean blind.
Do NOT ignore low-severity trends during busy periods.
